# Worst-Case Scenario Analysis

Phase 7B.2: Phase 7A.3's one-at-a-time sensitivity sweep varies exactly one Config-A/B parameter at a time. This analysis compounds every individually-adverse parameter value simultaneously (P-013/P-014/P-015 at the less-favorable end of their Phase 7A.3 range, P-019 included for completeness despite its documented null result), plus a data-arrival-rate storm on top -- see this module's docstring for the exact overrides and the direction rationale for each.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | 91.85% | 2.61% | 39819.86 | 0.000338873 |
| worst-case | 47.34% | 0.37% | 40089.54 | 0.000327397 |

Compounding every individually-adverse parameter value, plus a data-arrival storm, changes delivery success rate by -44.51 percentage points for config-a relative to baseline -- this is the honest floor a one-at-a-time sweep cannot show.

## Interpretation

A one-at-a-time sweep can miss compounding effects: two individually-modest degradations can interact (e.g. a stricter elevation mask shortens each pass window at the same time a longer safe-mode dwell reduces how many passes are even reached in comms-mode) to produce a worse outcome than either alone would predict by simple addition. Reporting this combined scenario alongside the one-at-a-time sweep gives an honest worst-case floor for this project's headline delivery-success-rate claim, not just a set of independent single-parameter perturbations.

## Battery and fault stress cases (not the reference scenario)

The reference scenario never reaches the 25% safe-mode entry threshold, so it never exercises SAFE_MODE. These cases perturb one sim-side quantity each (no config/*.yaml value changes) via sim.driver.run_simulation()'s stress knobs:

- **ST-1 depleted start**: initial SoC 25.2% (just above the 25% entry threshold) at the TLE epoch, which is in eclipse; single station.
- **ST-2 aged battery, two stations**: battery capacity 1.5 Wh (1/3 of the 4.5 Wh reference), dual station (more transmit bursts per orbit).
- **ST-3 injected fault**: fault_count = 3 (= every config's latched-fault threshold) for 1800 s starting at t = 8.35 h (inside the first pass); single station.

Reading the table. ST-1 and ST-3 give exactly one entry and one exit, and the exit shows the recovery model: Config A (P-014, 40%) and Config C (PC-012, 35%) recover autonomously, while Config B (ground-only, PB-010) waits for the next AOS (SIM-011). In ST-3 recovery is withheld until the injected fault clears. ST-2 enters SAFE_MODE inside passes and chatters: SIM-011 models ground as releasing SAFE_MODE at any in-pass tick regardless of SoC, so the next transmit burst re-triggers POWER_LOW within a tick or two. That is an artefact of the SIM-011 ground-operator assumption, not of the FSM; a SoC-aware ground release rule would remove it.
